R.C. Sproul
ar see sprohl
proper noun (figure)
Robert Charles Sproul (1939-2017), American Reformed theologian. Robert (Germanic, "bright fame"); Sproul, a Scottish surname. Usually styled "R.C. Sproul."

📖 Biblical Definition

Robert Charles Sproul (1939-2017) was the American Reformed theologian, teacher, and broadcaster whose gift for clear, compelling instruction made him one of the most influential popularizers of Reformed theology in the late 20th and early 21st centuries. Sproul founded Ligonier Ministries (1971), an immense teaching ministry whose conferences, broadcasts (the daily Renewing Your Mind program), and publications brought Reformed doctrine to a vast audience. His most famous book, The Holiness of God (1985), recovered for a generation the biblical vision of God's transcendent holiness and the creature's proper trembling before it, built around Isaiah's vision in the temple (Isa 6). He defended biblical inerrancy as a principal framer of the Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy (1978), classical apologetics, justification by faith alone (he was a leading critic of "Evangelicals and Catholics Together" precisely to defend sola fide), and the doctrines of grace (his Chosen by God made the Reformed doctrine of election accessible to ordinary readers). Sproul also founded Reformation Bible College and pastored Saint Andrew's Chapel in Florida. His teaching combined doctrinal precision with a rare clarity and an evident delight in the truth; he could make the hardest doctrines — election, the holiness of God, the atonement — both intelligible and weighty for the layman. Through Ligonier he equipped a generation of believers in confessional Reformed theology. The dictionary honors Sproul as the great modern teacher who made Reformed doctrine clear without making it shallow, and who defended the gospel distinctives of the Reformation in his own day.

R.C. SPROUL, proper noun. American Reformed theologian, teacher, and broadcaster (1939-2017).

Founder of Ligonier Ministries (1971) and the Renewing Your Mind broadcast; founder of Reformation Bible College.

Author of The Holiness of God (1985), Chosen by God, and many other works.

A principal framer of the Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy (1978); a classical apologist.

A leading critic of "Evangelicals and Catholics Together" in defense of justification by faith alone; pastor of Saint Andrew's Chapel.

Isaiah 6:5 — "Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips... for mine eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

R.C. Sproul is corrupted when his gift for clarity is mistaken for shallowness, when his popularizing role is set against scholarship as though accessible doctrine were lesser doctrine, or when his defenses of inerrancy and sola fide are forgotten behind his fame as a broadcaster.

expand to see more

Clarity-as-shallowness misreading. Sproul made the hardest doctrines accessible to ordinary believers — election, the holiness of God, the atonement, inerrancy. Some mistake accessibility for shallowness, as though doctrine made clear must be doctrine made thin. The reverse is true: it takes deep mastery to teach a hard thing clearly, and Sproul's clarity rested on genuine theological depth and precision. He did not dumb down the doctrines; he opened them. The gift of making the weighty intelligible to the layman is a high and rare gift, not a lesser one.

Popularizer-versus-scholar misreading. Because Sproul's primary calling was teaching the church rather than producing academic monographs, he is sometimes filed as a mere popularizer, beneath the serious theologians. This misjudges both the man and the calling. Sproul was a careful theologian who chose to spend his gifts equipping the ordinary believer — a calling the church desperately needs and too often despises. Through Ligonier he did more to ground a generation in confessional Reformed theology than many a scholar reaching only the academy. The dictionary honors the teacher of the church as highly as the teacher of the academy.
